summary.native: to have and not give back; to stay or make stay in a state; to continue; to store; to do what you promised

etymology.ko: 고대 영어 후기의 cepan('붙잡다, 지니다; 바라다, 지켜 행하다')에서 왔다. 게르만 조어 *kopjan으로 거슬러 올라가지만 그 너머의 기원은 분명하지 않다. 고대 영어 capian('보다')과 관련이 있다는 견해가 있어, 본래 뜻이 '눈을 떼지 않고 지켜보다'였을 것으로 보기도 한다. 중세 영어 시기에 '지키다, 돌보다, 막다, 간직하다, 계속 머무르다' 같은 뜻이 잇따라 생겼다.
etymology.native: From late Old English cepan, 'to seize, hold; to seek, observe'. It goes back to Proto-Germanic *kopjan, whose origin is uncertain. Some connect it with Old English capian, 'to look', so the first idea may have been 'to keep an eye on'. In Middle English it gained many senses, such as guard, look after, prevent, preserve, and stay.

grammar.ko: 불규칙 동사다: keep - kept - kept. -ing형은 keeping이다.
grammar.native: Irregular verb: keep, kept, kept. The -ing form is keeping.

grammar.ko: '계속 ~하다'는 keep + -ing 또는 keep on + -ing로 쓴다. keep + to부정사는 쓰지 않는다(keep to study는 틀림).
grammar.native: For 'continue doing', use keep + -ing or keep on + -ing. Keep is not followed by a to-infinitive in this sense.

grammar.ko: keep + 목적어 + 형용사·분사·부사로 '~을 어떤 상태로 두다'를 나타낸다: keep the room clean, keep me waiting.
grammar.native: Keep + object + adjective, participle, or adverb means 'make something stay in a state': keep the room clean, keep me waiting.

grammar.ko: keep A from -ing는 'A가 ~하지 못하게 하다'다: The rain kept us from going out.
grammar.native: Keep A from -ing means 'stop A from doing something': The rain kept us from going out.

grammar.ko: 자주 쓰는 구동사·표현: keep up with(뒤처지지 않다), keep out(들이지 않다), keep away from(멀리하다), keep in touch(연락하고 지내다).
grammar.native: Common phrasal verbs and phrases: keep up with (not fall behind), keep out, keep away from, keep in touch (stay in contact).

meaning.ko: (돌려주지 않고) 가지다, 계속 가지고 있다, 간직하다
meaning.native: to have something and not give it back or throw it away

usage.ko: 받은 것이나 가진 것을 돌려주거나 버리지 않고 자기 것으로 둘 때 쓴다. Keep the change.(잔돈은 가지세요)는 아주 흔한 표현이다.
usage.native: Used when you continue to have something instead of returning it or throwing it away. Keep the change is a very common phrase.

examples.text: You can keep the book. I've already read it.
examples.ko: 그 책은 가져도 돼. 난 벌써 읽었어.

examples.text: Here's 20 dollars. Keep the change.
I kept all the letters she sent me.
examples.ko: 나는 그녀가 보낸 편지를 모두 간직했다.

meaning.native: to stay in a particular state, or to make someone or something stay in it

usage.ko: keep + 형용사(계속 ~한 상태로 있다), keep + 목적어 + 형용사(~을 계속 ~하게 두다)로 쓴다. 조용히, 따뜻하게, 깨끗하게처럼 상태를 이어 갈 때 쓴다.
usage.native: Used as keep + adjective (stay in a state) or keep + object + adjective (make something stay in a state), for things like quiet, warm, and clean.

examples.text: Please keep the door closed.
Keep quiet. The baby is sleeping.
This coat will keep you warm all winter.
examples.ko: 이 코트를 입으면 겨울 내내 따뜻할 거야.

meaning.native: to continue doing something, or to do it again and again

usage.ko: keep + -ing로 멈추지 않고 이어 하거나 같은 일이 되풀이됨을 나타낸다. 되풀이되는 일에는 짜증이 담길 때가 많다.
usage.native: Used as keep + -ing to show that something continues or happens again and again. Repeated actions often suggest annoyance.

examples.text: Keep going straight, and you'll see the bank on your right.
My phone keeps turning off by itself.
Don't give up. Keep trying!

meaning.native: to store something in a particular place

usage.ko: 물건을 늘 두는 자리, 보관하는 곳을 말할 때 쓴다. 장소는 in, on 같은 전치사로 나타낸다.
usage.native: Used to say where something is usually stored. The place follows a preposition such as in or on.

collocations: keep something in a safe place

examples.text: Where do you keep the paper for the printer?
I keep my passport in a safe place.
We keep old files in the storage room.

meaning.native: to do what you promised, or not to tell a secret

usage.ko: 약속한 대로 하거나 비밀을 남에게 말하지 않을 때 쓴다. 반대로 약속을 어기다는 break a promise다.
usage.native: Used for doing what you said you would, or not telling a secret. The opposite of keep a promise is break a promise.

examples.text: He always keeps his promises.
Can you keep a secret?
I'm sorry I couldn't keep our appointment yesterday.
examples.ko: 어제 만나기로 한 약속을 못 지켜서 죄송합니다.

meaning.ko: (사람을) 붙잡아 두다, 늦게 하다; (keep from) ~하지 못하게 하다
meaning.native: to make someone stay or be late, or (keep from) to stop someone from doing something

usage.ko: 누군가를 붙잡아 시간을 뺏거나 늦게 만들 때 쓴다. What kept you?(왜 늦었어?)가 흔하다. keep A from -ing는 A가 ~하지 못하게 막는다는 뜻이다.
usage.native: Used when something holds a person up or makes them late, as in What kept you? Keep A from -ing means stopping A from doing something.

examples.text: You're an hour late! What kept you?
examples.ko: 한 시간이나 늦었잖아! 왜 이렇게 늦었어?

examples.text: I won't keep you long. I just have one question.
The noise upstairs kept me from sleeping last night.
examples.ko: 어젯밤 위층 소음 때문에 잠을 못 잤다.

meaning.native: to write down information regularly, such as in a diary or a record

usage.ko: 일기·장부·명단처럼 날마다 또는 꾸준히 적어 나가는 기록에 쓴다. write a diary보다 keep a diary가 자연스럽다.
usage.native: Used for records you write regularly, such as a diary, accounts, or a list. Keep a diary is more natural than write a diary.

examples.text: I keep a diary in English to practice writing.
examples.ko: 나는 글쓰기 연습을 하려고 영어로 일기를 쓴다.

examples.text: Please keep a record of your travel costs.
Our office keeps a list of all visitors.
examples.ko: 우리 사무실은 방문객을 빠짐없이 명단에 적어 둔다.

meaning.native: (of food) to stay fresh and good to eat

usage.ko: 목적어 없이 쓰며, 음식이 얼마나 오래 상하지 않는지 말할 때 쓴다. 주로 well, for + 기간, until과 함께 온다.
usage.native: Used without an object to say how long food stays fresh. It often comes with well, for + a period of time, or until.

examples.text: Cooked rice doesn't keep well in summer.
This kimchi will keep for months in the fridge.
examples.ko: 이 김치는 냉장고에서 몇 달은 간다.

examples.text: Eat the fish today. It won't keep until tomorrow.
examples.ko: 생선은 오늘 먹어. 내일까지 못 가.

cautions.ko: 한국어 '약속'을 모두 promise로 옮기면 틀린다. promise는 '~하겠다는 다짐'이고, 만날 약속은 plans나 appointment다. 오늘 약속이 있다는 I have plans today.라고 한다.
cautions.native: A promise is saying you will do something. For a meeting with someone, use plans or an appointment: I have plans today, not I have a promise today.

cautions.ko: '자리 좀 맡아 줘'는 save나 hold가 가장 흔하다: Could you save my seat? keep을 쓸 때는 keep a seat for me처럼 for + 사람을 붙인다. Keep your seat.는 '일어나지 말고 앉아 계세요'라는 뜻이다.
cautions.native: To ask someone to save a place for you, say Could you save my seat? or Could you keep a seat for me? Keep your seat means 'stay sitting down'.

cautions.ko: keep + -ing는 '계속'뿐 아니라 '자꾸, 또'라는 불만의 느낌도 준다. You keep interrupting me.는 '자꾸 말을 끊으시네요'라는 항의다.
cautions.native: Keep + -ing can show annoyance about something repeated. You keep interrupting me is a complaint, not a neutral fact.

note.ko: 어떤 상태를 이어 간다는 뜻이다. quiet, calm, warm처럼 상태를 말하는 형용사가 온다.
note.native: Means to stay in a state, with adjectives such as quiet, calm, or warm.

patterns.example: Keep still while I take the photo.

note.ko: 무엇을 어떤 상태로 두라는 틀이다. 목적어 뒤에 형용사나 분사가 온다.
note.native: Means to leave something in a certain state. An adjective or a participle follows the object.

patterns.example: Please keep the gate closed at night.

note.ko: 계속 또는 자꾸 한다는 뜻이다. 불만을 담아 말할 때도 쓴다.
note.native: Means to continue, or to do something again and again, sometimes with a note of complaint.

patterns.example: My phone keeps turning itself off.

note.ko: 누가 어떤 일을 하지 못하게 막는다는 뜻이다. from 뒤에 -ing가 온다.
note.native: Means to stop a person from doing something. The -ing form follows from.

patterns.example: The noise kept me from falling asleep.

difference.ko: maintain은 기계나 건물을 손봐 가며 유지한다는 격식 있는 말이다. 상태를 그대로 두는 것은 keep이다.
difference.native: Maintain is a formal word for looking after a machine or a building so it stays in order, while keep is simply staying in a state.

confusables.example: They maintain the road, and we keep the yard clean.

difference.ko: store는 쓰지 않는 것을 어딘가에 쌓아 둔다는 뜻이다. keep은 평소에 두는 자리까지 뜻한다.
difference.native: Store means putting things away until they are needed, while keep also covers where something normally lives.

confusables.example: We store the tents in the attic and keep the tools in the shed.

difference.ko: hold는 지금 쥐고 있다는 뜻이고, keep은 돌려주지 않고 계속 가진다는 뜻이다. 거스름돈은 keep으로 말한다.
difference.native: Hold means having something in your hands now, while keep means not giving it back. At a shop you say Keep the change.

confusables.example: Hold my bag, and keep the receipt for me.
